title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for intent→configuration artifacts produced by a declared model (gpt-5-mini, provider recorded as openai_responses) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a deterministic task bank and abstracted vendor‑CLI families, Npairs = 720 complete paired episodes were analyzed. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 (0.9986111111111111); the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation, with at most one repair-stage call per task) flagged 720/720 (1.0). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair). These artifact-grounded numbers lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, an artifact-grounded primary analysis, a concise clarification of provider-call/audit accounting, and an evidence-based interpretation that attributes the near-zero aggregate guarded benefit to validator ceiling effects in this curated regime.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, command-order/workflow constraints, and higher-order safety or policy invariants. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document this workflow-centred mitigation pattern and motivate rigorous, paired measurements of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to answer: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation (permitted one repair-stage model call per task)? Primary contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and autonomous execution that adhered to the preregistered contract; (2) a fully artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720; (3) an explicit clarification of provider-call/audit accounting that resolves apparent asymmetries in reported model-call counts; (4) an artifact-grounded interpretation explaining why the guarded-stage marginal effect was negligible in this experimental regime and where guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Multiple recent surveys and architecture reports synthesize the trend of pairing LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to increase operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1], [2]. Tool-focused case studies emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional—syntactic parsing, workflow ordering, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties each require different V&V primitives. Practical prototypes and tools (e.g., configuration-analysis systems and topology-aware verifiers) have expanded rule sets and checks but still exhibit gaps for runtime-dependent behaviors and stateful sequences; these gaps motivate adding sandboxed emulation in some deployments [2], [3].

Empirical positioning. Prior prototypes show heterogeneous gains from emulation: in some task regimes a verifier already catches most dangerous errors, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures or environment-specific side effects that static rules miss. Our paired design (shared_initial_candidate semantics) isolates only downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or permitted repair invocations) and therefore complements prior system and survey evidence with an auditable, preregistered numeric estimate for a constrained task distribution.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered sampling plan targeted Npairs = 720 with a minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 for power planning. Key preregistered decisions included: shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled generation per task reused across paired conditions), deterministic task generation and parser-based inclusion, deterministic missingness handling (up to two automatic reseeds for parser failures), and a repair policy allowing at most one repair-stage model invocation per task.

Task bank, topology templates, and validators. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from intent_configuration_repair_v1. The bank covers three abstracted vendor‑CLI families and several topology templates (leaf–spine, 3‑node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest includes initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change, minimum_active_in_groups). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after allowed reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory run (complete_pair_count = 720).

Model and generation semantics. The declared/requested model was recorded as gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); the client did not set an explicit temperature (recorded as null in the model configuration). Shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: each pair used exactly one provider-sampled initial candidate, and that identical candidate was presented to both downstream conditions. This isolates guarded-stage signals from generation variability.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements deterministic rule-based checks: vendor-CLI syntactic parsing, command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints, protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology, applies normalized CLI commands to vendor-abstracted virtual devices, and produces runtime observations (interface transitions, transient downtimes, MTU/VLAN application effects, reachability consequences). Emulation observations are mapped to runtime-observation rules that can trigger additional detections not codified as static validator violations. The guarded repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model call per task, invoked only after emulation observations were available.

Provider-call audit fields and reconciliation (clarification requested by reviewers). The execution manifest records provider-call audit fields that count model-call events, not per-condition episode invocations. Two audit fields require explicit mapping: (1) stage_counts reports model calls by pipeline stage (e.g., shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1). This shows we performed one shared initial generation per pair and a single repair-stage invocation in the entire confirmatory run. (2) condition_counts in the provider audit reflect additional per-stage call attributions (for example, a nonzero guarded key appears when a repair-stage call is attributed to the guarded workflow). The apparent asymmetry between episode counts (complete_pair_count = 720, completed_episode_count = 1440) and model-call condition_counts arises because the identical shared initial generation was used by both conditions (counted once as a shared model call) whereas the single repair-stage call was executed only in the guarded pipeline and therefore appears under the guarded attribution. In short: audit counts enumerate model-call events by stage and attribution; pair/episode accounting enumerates paired executions. The manifest-level reconciliation confirms model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair) and complete_pair_count = 720; these two perspectives are consistent when interpreted as model-call events vs. episode pairs.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis used a preregistered paired-binary executor (McNemar-style exact two-sided test) and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The primary analysis used complete-pair handling (no irrecoverable technical pairs were present). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory with multiplicity correction but are not the focus of the confirmatory claim.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential summary (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts were: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These numeric results are taken verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts used by the paired-binary executor.

Discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation recorded stage_counts showing a single repair-stage call and model_calls_used = 721. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, any guarded-only detection (n10) must originate from either (i) an emulation-only observation not codified as a static validator rule, or (ii) a repair-stage invocation that altered the candidate after the shared initial generation. The archived reconciliation links the unique n10 to the single recorded repair-stage call; auditors can locate the discordant pair in the canonical raw-results artifact by searching for the single entry where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1. This mapping is reported without pasting per-episode logs but is supported by the archived manifest-level reconciliation that attributes the single extra model call to the guarded repair stage.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces (validator_trace objects) show that most shared_initial candidates matched the required command sequences and violated no validator rules (violation_count = 0) for the curated task bank. The observed ceiling in validator coverage (baseline success = 719/720) leaves essentially no headroom for emulation to produce additional detections at scale in this regime.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage marginal benefit negligible? The artifact-grounded evidence supports three primary factors.

Validator ceiling effect. The deterministic validator explicitly encodes the workflow constraints exercised by the curated tasks (e.g., shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Representative validator_trace fields show parsed_command_count matching required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for nearly all shared_initial candidates; with baseline success at 99.861%, there is minimal headroom for emulation to add detections on this task distribution.

Curated parser-validated task bank. Inclusion required parser acceptance and deterministic task generation; as a result the confirmatory set intentionally excluded noisy or adversarially malformed inputs. This reduces the prevalence of runtime-only faults that emulation typically surfaces in broader or adversarial distributions.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. By reusing the identical sampled initial candidate across both conditions, observed discordance can only arise downstream of generation. Provider-call auditing confirms only a single repair-stage call occurred across the 720 pairs, and the unique n10 maps to that event. Thus the guarded pipeline was not able to leverage per-condition re-generation opportunities to correct or avoid faults in this design; any guarded advantage had to come from emulation observations or that single repair-stage call.

Operational implications. For operator regimes that maintain a high-coverage static validator tuned to expected intent patterns and enforce parser-based inclusion, adding an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may yield negligible incremental detection benefit. This does not negate the value of emulation in other regimes: noisy natural-language intents, broader vendor/CLI diversity, adversarial misconfigurations, or long-lived stateful interactions are plausible settings where guarded stages provide substantive gains. Practically, operators should (a) invest in validator coverage for high-throughput low-latency paths, (b) selectively apply guarded sandboxing for high-impact changes, and (c) use adversarial/fuzzing banks to discover validator gaps; the archived traces here can seed such follow-up design work.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator against the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline provided a negligible aggregated detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call reconciliation shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair), and the single guarded-only discordance maps to the single repair-stage call under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We interpret this near-zero aggregate effect as a validator ceiling effect for this curated regime; generalization to adversarial or production-like regimes requires targeted follow-up using adversarial task banks, broader vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation. The archived execution and analysis artifacts permit independent verification of the numeric claims and the discordant-pair attribution described above (see Reproducibility).

Execution and analysis were performed autonomously after the lock: literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting were produced by the agentic pipeline. The canonical archived execution manifest and analysis bundle (the artifact bundle referenced by the preregistration) contain the per-episode raw results, provider-call audit, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts used to produce all numeric claims—consult that archive for full per-file provenance.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce constrained ecological diversity and created a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability and potential re-generation benefits.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite manifest-level reconciliation; these residuals are documented in the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
